title: Prove weighted periodic Gaussian power bound and reduce complete inverse to120 terms
body:
The original complete periodic Gaussian inverse service used276 terms because its tail estimate inherited the small scalar row gap. This contribution proves a source-compatible diagonal majorant for the actual rational reference across shared ratios, cross-cell entries, period crossings and holes. The weighted contraction is independent of theta, while its exponential gauge prefactor remains explicit.

On the unchanged `Reference(384,1,2,4,18,320)`, the complete action now uses120 terms/119 updates on the same33-bit grid, down from276 terms/275 updates. The full385-row output, numerical rounding, coefficient error, inherited analytic perturbation, setup caches, output ownership and cleanup remain funded. The new trajectory performs731,136 integer products and91,630 component roundings. This is a host-array consumer saving, not a physical tape, production-family or multiplication-bound claim.

Validation regenerates all3,457 original source entries, checks the exact original-reference residual, preserves every wrap and hole, and executes a dropped-wrap trajectory whose residual yields a genuine error lower bound above the target. Normal generation passed33.329s; the strengthened negative control passed independently in0.68s. The final committed Git-free, read-only optimized replay passed33.23s; real missing-RESULT, missing-SOURCES, Boolean-bill and source-corruption mutations were rejected, with all export bytes restored exactly. Independent proof review covers the all-branch inequality, rational-weight inflation and complete numerical budget.

Sources and predecessor credit are pinned in SOURCES.json. See PROOF.md for quantified hypotheses and the complete setup/workspace invoice; VERIFY.json registers reproduction. The remaining production question is whether an admitted caller can pay the retained gauge, setup and physical delivery costs. No selected frontier is changed.

Prepared by JoyboyBrian with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit Jose Manuel, Vlado Vojdanovski, Jeremy Kothe, Cinna Davis, Mason Hale, James Reed and the retained Gaussian/precision lineage; Apache-2.0 and predecessor attribution retained.
